items.title: Bob Lovett Interview, 1949-04-01
items.q: It was himself and there was a piano player named Sweet William, I believe.

ctx.x: G-E-R-O-U-L-D. It seemed to me that if anybody could sit in, there weren't many restrictions. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. That's right, yeah. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. So, Lee had what? Three, four pieces?

G-E-R-O-U-L-D. It was himself and there was a piano player named Sweet William, I believe. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Yes. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Actually, I think his name was William Sweet. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Oh, oh. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Yeah, but everybody used to call him Sweet. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. And I don't know if he had a regular drummer there or not.

G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Freddie Flynn? Do you remember that? G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Yes, I remember the name. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Freddie Flynn, frequently drummed for him. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. All right, I'd like to stop this for a moment. . . . . Thank you. Thank you. Thank you. Thank you. Thank you. Thank you. Thank you. Thank you. Thank you. Thank you. Thank you. Thank you. Thank you. Thank you.
